The October edition of the GraphQL over HTTP Working Group meeting focused on the release status of the specification and two potential registrations: status code 294 for partial content and a new media type application/GraphQL response plus JSON. Benjie confirmed that the specification is ready for release pending final approval from the TSC chair, and the team agreed to create a new next branch rather than merging directly to main. The group discussed whether to register the new status code and media type with IANA, with Martin suggesting it would be beneficial to engage with the broader HTTP community. Benjie advised waiting for wider ecosystem adoption before pursuing IANA registration, particularly for the status code, as the current use case may not justify allocating a new HTTP status code in the 200s range. The team also briefly discussed Miguel's work on creating a GraphQL over HTTP Rust implementation and his involvement in other open source projects.

## Summary

### GraphQL Working Group Scheduling

The meeting began with participants discussing scheduling confusion, particularly regarding the AI working group meeting that Miguel had incorrectly scheduled for the wrong day. Martin and Benjie clarified that the AI working group met on the fourth Thursday of the month, and suggested using calendar.graphql.org for accurate scheduling. ### GraphQL Specification Release Status

The team discussed the status of a GraphQL specification release that is pending final approval from the TSC chair. Benjie explained that while the specification has sufficient votes to meet TSC criteria, it needs the TSC chair's formal approval before being published. The team agreed to create a new "next" branch for development work instead of merging directly into main until the release is completed and shipped.

### GraphQL HTTP Status Code Discussion

The team discussed registering a new HTTP status code 294 for partial content in GraphQL, which would allow returning some data while indicating errors on other fields. Benjie and Miguel agreed that while the concept makes sense, they don't expect 294 to be approved as it's too specific to GraphQL, and suggested looking at existing similar status codes like 207 multi-status. Benjie recommended waiting for wider ecosystem adoption before pursuing IETF registration, as the current need may not be unique enough to GraphQL to warrant a new status code.

### GraphQL HTTP Status Code 294

The group discussed the implementation of a new HTTP status code 294 for "partial success" in GraphQL over HTTP. Benjie emphasized that the status code should be based on actual usage data rather than speculation, and explained how current systems handle GraphQL responses by inferring status from JSON structure. The team agreed on "partial success" as an appropriate name for the status code, and discussed whether to register a media type for GraphQL responses, with Benjie questioning the necessity given that the GraphQL Foundation already defines the behavior.

### Media Type Registration Discussion

The team discussed registering a media type for their specification similar to what AsyncAPI has already done. Martin noted that AsyncAPI has a registered media type (application/asyncapi+json) under the Linux Foundation's initiative, and while there are no specific objections to registering their own type, they would need to consider the time and resources required. Martin plans to discuss this with other API standards groups at an upcoming event in Paris to understand the registration process and determine the best approach.

### GraphQL Specification Status Update

The team discussed the status of the GraphQL specification, with Benjie confirming that the current pull request represents the final version that will be released as 1.0 in September 2026. Miguel shared his experience creating a GraphQL-Rust crate and mentioned his involvement in other projects including OpenAPI and OpenLint. Benjie mentioned his work on the Golden Path project, which aims to establish guidelines for clients and servers, and noted that standardized linting tools would be beneficial for the ecosystem.
